The gate failed because of systematic ENCODING MISMATCH on five content checks. C6 (0/3, linked to PF1) expects a commitment type resembling "capacity-guardrail," but models naturally produce types like "configuration," "rollout_configuration," or "enforcement." C7 (0/3, linked to PF2) expects a commitment type resembling "tenant-region-filter," but models produce "verification," "rollout_configuration," or "documentation." C8 (0/3, linked to PF3) expects a commitment type resembling "human-review," but models produce "configuration," "rollout_configuration," or "documentation." C2 (0/3, linked to PF2) never passes despite settlements correctly stating non-EU tenants with EU exclusion, suggesting the check's expected string for eligible_tenant_group does not match any natural model phrasing. C5 (2/3, linked to PF3) failed only in rollout 0, where the escalation channel was encoded as "CS beta escalation channel" instead of "Customer Success beta escalation channel," indicating the check requires the full spelling. Rollout 3 auto-failed at 18 turns with all facts revealed by turn 7—a structural problem where the facilitator (A1) kept asking follow-up questions and deferring the settle decision rather than recognizing it had enough information to settle.

Does that timeline work for everyone, and are there any objections to the proposed approach?
